science.title: Chronobiology applied to your trip
science.p1: Light is the main synchronizer of the body clock. Depending on the biological time at which it is received, it advances or delays that clock.
science.p2: That is why exposure to light at the wrong time can slow down adaptation to the new time zone. Fuseo uses your route, the direction of travel and your usual sleep hours to determine the relevant windows.
science.prcTitle: Same light, opposite effect depending on timing
science.delayText: delays the clock (useful when flying west)
science.advanceText: advances the clock (useful when flying east)
science.prcNote: The “biological morning” follows your internal clock, not local time: right after a long flight, it can fall in the middle of the afternoon.

footer.disclaimer: Fuseo provides general information and advice on sleep and travel chronobiology. The service is not a medical consultation, does not make a diagnosis and does not replace the advice of a healthcare professional. It is intended for healthy adults. If you are pregnant, have a chronic illness, bipolar disorder, an eye disease or are undergoing treatment, ask your doctor before following a plan.

team.storyLead: Sleep expertise, now accessible to all travelers.
team.story1: It all began at the Institut Médical du Sommeil in Paris.
team.story2: In our practice, we worked with people facing exceptional demands: elite athletes, executives, frequent international travelers, and patients for whom jet lag was a real difficulty.
team.story3: They all asked the same question: how can I arrive feeling well instead of spending the first days recovering?
team.story4: We saw that advice to sleep on the plane or get daylight was not enough. Jet lag is more complex. Light at the wrong time, a poorly timed nap or unsuitable advice can delay adjustment of the body clock.
team.story5: AI can produce recommendations in seconds, but it does not by itself guarantee that they make sense in chronobiological terms.
team.story7: For months, we studied scientific models of the body clock, compared approaches, examined their limits and designed an algorithm to turn that knowledge into personal guidance.
team.story8: Our aim was simple: make this expertise available beyond the few travelers receiving specialist support.
team.story9: Why not let everyone benefit from it?
team.story10: That is how Fuseo was born.
team.scienceBehindText: Our method explains the scientific models and chronobiology principles behind each plan.

planner.lifestyleNote: Alcohol: none in the 4 hours before bed, and none on board. Smoking: nothing in the 2 hours before bed; for a long flight, ask your pharmacist about nicotine replacement. Intense exercise: finished at least 2 hours before bed.

planner.itemMealF: Meal on board, on destination time
planner.mealNote: Meals: eat on destination time from the flight onwards; if the onboard service falls during your sleep, sleep instead. Have a light dinner (not too fatty or spicy) at least 3 h before bed; a light snack is fine. Drink water regularly in the cabin.

planner.adviceNote: General information: it does not replace your doctor's advice.

advice.pregnant: Pregnancy: no alcohol or melatonin; coffee limited to 2 cups a day and stopped early (10 h before bed). On the flight, walk every 1 to 2 hours and drink water. Before a long flight, ask your midwife or doctor.
advice.minor: Under 18: no alcohol, no coffee 'boost', no melatonin without medical advice.
advice.heart: Heart rhythm disorder or high blood pressure: the plan does not suggest coffee 'boosts'. On the flight, stand up regularly and stay hydrated; ask your doctor before a long trip.
advice.apnea: Sleep apnoea: no alcohol in the evening (at least 6 h before bed) and no sleeping pills. If you use a CPAP machine, carry it in the cabin and check with the airline whether it can be used on board.
advice.bipolar: Bipolar disorder: jet lag and bright light can destabilise mood. No light-therapy lamp without medical advice; tell your psychiatrist before the trip and keep regular sleep times.
advice.eye: Eye condition or light-sensitising medicine: no light-therapy lamp without medical advice. Prefer daylight, with your usual protection.
advice.pill: Contraceptive pill: caffeine is cleared more slowly, so the coffee cut-off is 2 h earlier. Also think about your pill time across time zones: follow the leaflet or ask your pharmacist.
advice.senior: 65 and over: your clock is often earlier and slightly less sensitive to light; the plan takes this into account. Seek real daylight (outdoors) and keep naps short (20 minutes). Coffee stops 1 h earlier.
advice.fifty: 50 and over: sleep becomes more sensitive to evening coffee; the cut-off is 1 h earlier.
advice.smoker: Smoking: it is forbidden on board and in most airports, and nicotine withdrawal can fragment sleep on the flight. Ask your pharmacist about nicotine replacement.
